Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Light Up a Life 2026 — draft for Moira to see

Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the window again this year.

Memory tags will be on the counter here in the shop from Monday 16 November. There's a suggested donation of £3, and if you'd rather write yours at home there are envelopes on the counter you can take away and bring back.

The tree goes into the window on Saturday 21 November, and we'll switch the lights on at 4pm on Saturday 28 November. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing a few carols, and Doreen is doing mince pies again. Last year they didn't survive the first carol, so come early.

This is the seventh year since Ray died at the hospice, in November 2019. The first year I hung his tag I could hardly write it. I sat with the pen for a long time and got about as far as his name. Now I write it at the counter, with the same pen, and it takes me a minute. I'm telling you that because I know what it's like to stand there not knowing how to begin, and because I'd like you to know that nobody here minds if it takes you a while.

The tree isn't only for hospice families. It's for anyone grieving, anyone at all, and you don't have to have lost someone this year, or have been cared for by us, or explain yourself to anybody.

And you don't need to buy anything. You can just come in and stand by the tree for a bit. Nobody will ask you for anything, and if you'd rather come when it's quiet, mornings are usually best.

Every name on every tag will be read aloud at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You don't have to come to the service for your name to be read — it will be read either way — and you'd be very welcome if you do come.

Last year the tree carried 412 names, and I want to thank everyone who wrote one, and everyone who came in just to look. Thank you for trusting us with them.

Jean

Subject: Light Up a Life post

Moira, the post is drafted and sitting on the page for you — please have a read before it goes up and tell me what you'd change.

I've left the totals out of it this year. I'd rather thank people for the names than for the money, if you don't mind; 412 of them is thanks enough to be going on with.

There's a short reply drafted under Hilary Gotts's question as well, just confirming the dates, since she was asking about her mum. Have a look at that too while you're there.

Jean
